Sam - Update chargeback spreadsheet with Dedicated usage data - due 2026-11-27
Riley - Share KMS rotation plan and Custody matrix - due 2026-11-23
Alex - Confirm on-prem patch window with data center ops - due 2026-11-25

next_steps: Maya to send SSO rollout comms to all engineering and product teams
Riley to post KMS rotation doc in #security-ops and attach to ticket

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-20 | Start: 09:30 PT | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (IT), Sam Patel (Finance Ops), Riley Ortega (Security), Alex Gomez (Infra), Leah Ford (Ops), Chris Tan (SRE), Jordan Lee (Legal), Priya Nair (Procurement), Nina Brooks (Facilities), Tom Avery (Accounting)
Link: https://redwood-internal/notes/it-finance-security-2026-11-20 (doc)

[00:00] Maya: okay uh let's get started, thanks everyone for hopping on. I think we have most folks. Quick agenda, sso rollout, kms rotation, finance chargebacks for dedicated, on-prem patching window, audit logs questions. Anything to add?
[00:22] Sam: no that's fine, I just want to make sure we have the new usage numbers for dedicated capacity before we talk chargebacks.
[00:36] Riley: and I'll need to confirm the key rotation cadence, there's a little bit of overlap with procurement for HSM leases.
[00:50] Alex: also we should mention the data center has a maintenance slot next week, could conflict with the patch window.
[01:05] Maya: great, okay first SSO. We're aiming to start phased rollouts with SAML next Monday across dev and staging, target prod in three weeks. This is the plan we shared, link in the doc. There were a couple of outstanding items from infra - Alex you had an open question on session timeout?
[01:30] Alex: yeah the default session is 24 hours with Okta, but some teams asked for shorter, also on the service side we need to ensure token refresh works with our redirect flows. We noticed one of the redirect URIs was mis-typed in the dev config, so that's on us to fix.
[01:54] Leah: is there a plan to black-out any dashboards during the rollout? We had some alerts flare during last friday's config change.
[02:10] Chris: we can put a brief maintenance window per environment, like 30 minutes for staging and 1 hour for prod, but we shouldn't block telemetry entirely. We'll annotate the dashboards.
[02:32] Maya: okay action - Maya will draft the comms with timeline and blackout windows.
[02:45] Sam: on the finance side, I'm pulling usage for dedicated pools. FYI the accounting team wants the chargeback model to include a 10% ops overhead, and that was debated in last week's call.
[03:05] Tom: yeah accounting prefers a predictable monthly rate rather than per-minute billing for Dedicated in the enterprise customers so we need to show forecasted spend.
[03:20] Maya: do we have the current utilization numbers?
[03:30] Sam: pulled them, but I need to clean the sample \u2014 there were spiking ks during benchmarks, a couple of POC jobs skewed the numbers. I'll filter those out and send an updated sheet.
[03:50] Maya: perfect, include Alex if we need any low-level logs.
[04:03] Riley: moving to KMS rotation \u2014 team, current plan is quarterly rotation for data-plane keys, yearly rotation for master keys, using our KMS with HSM integration. But procurement flagged costs for additional HSM slots if we increase frequency.
[04:26] Priya: procurement here, yeah we can negotiate terms but HSM capacity is billed per slot, we need a solid justification. Is quarterly rotation a hard requirement?
[04:40] Riley: it's a best practice, but we can do tiered: quarterly for sensitive data (payments, legal hold) and semi-annual for others. Jordan, any legal input?
[04:55] Jordan: legal is okay with tiered approach, we just need the custody and access matrix documented. Also we may need to put certain keys on longer retention for eDiscovery.
[05:12] Maya: Riley will share the KMS rotation doc and a custody matrix.
[05:22] Riley: yup I'll post it in #security-ops and attach the doc link. Expect questions.
[05:35] Alex: one more infra note \u2014 the on-prem hosts will need a patch window. The DC ops team has an open slot next thursday night 22:00 PT to 02:00. That collides with some scheduled backups but we can move them.
[05:55] Nina: facilities here, confirm the window works from our side, power maintenance will be isolated to the backplane, we don't expect issues but we'll provide a runbook.
[06:12] Maya: let's tentatively take that window, Alex confirm with DC ops and post the runbook.
[06:24] Alex: will do.
[06:30] Sam: on chargebacks again, if we move to a monthly reserved charge for dedicated, procurement wants an SLA clause for unused capacity credits to roll forward, is that feasible?
[06:46] Maya: product side will need to build that feature but for internal accounting we can handle credits manually initially. We should track it as a liability line.
[06:58] Tom: accounting prefers explicit credits rather than manual adjustments for auditability.
[07:08] Jordan: speaking of audit, who currently has access to audit logs? We had a question from legal about retention for security investigations.
[07:22] Riley: logs are stored for 90 days in hot storage by default, 365 in cold. Legal can request extended retention for specific projects, but we need to document access procedures. There's a ticketing flow but it's a little ad-hoc.
[07:42] Jordan: could we get an SLA for evidence preservation on request? Even a 24-hour ack is fine, we just need consistency.
[07:55] Riley: yes we can commit to 24-hour ack, I'll add that to the runbook.
[08:05] Maya: quick note \u2014 Naomi on the platform team flagged that some product names are getting mis-spelled in the comms (Redwood Dedicate vs Dedicated), just FYI for the email.
[08:20] Sam: haha, will correct that. Also we had a question about tax treatment for reserved capacity \u2014 does procurement have a play here?
[08:31] Priya: procurement will coordinate with tax, usually it's capitalizable if we treat it as a committed contract, but we need the contract language.
[08:43] Maya: good. Any blockers on procurement?
[08:48] Priya: just the HSM slot negotiation and timing for new contracts; otherwise fine.
[08:56] Alex: small ops item \u2014 Chris and I noticed the KV cache metric spelled as KV cash in one of the dashboards, could be a transcription error in alerts, so update the metric name.
[09:12] Chris: yep caused a couple of false positives. I'll rename and ensure alert thresholds are sane.
[09:22] Leah: tiny thing \u2014 can we add a calendar invite for the maintenance window with the runbook link? saves confusion.
[09:30] Maya: yes will do once Alex confirms.
[09:36] Jordan: last legal point, when you send the SSO comms include a section about data export processes for employees leaving, we need to ensure HR and legal are looped.
[09:47] Maya: noted.
[09:50] Sam: i'll update the chargeback spreadsheet and send to everyone.
[09:57] Maya: okay recap: Maya draft SSO comms and calendar invites; Riley share KMS rotation + custody matrix and add 24-hr ack to runbook; Alex confirm DC ops window and post runbook; Sam clean usage and update chargeback model; Jordan review audit exceptions; Priya follow procurement on HSM terms. We'll meet next week same time unless something changes.
[10:20] Maya: thanks everyone, I'll send notes and action items after the call.
[10:25] (end)

Notes: transcription imperfect in a few spots (names and product spellings). References to shared docs above.
